newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banks rebound boosts Australia stocks to record close.
newsitem.headline: Banks rebound boosts Australia stocks to record close.

text.p: A resurgent banking sector, encouraged by news of unchanged U.S. interest rates, carried the Australian stock market to a record close on Wednesday.
"Buyers were coming back into the market looking for a bargain, in particular the banks," Reynolds and Co broker Peter Struk said.
"You're going to see the All Ords reach 2,600 before you'll see a decent pull-back," Struk said.
National Australia Bank jumped 38 cents to A$18.18 (US14.11) leading a bank-wide rally which pushed the banks and finance index up 83.3 points or 1.92 percent to 4,432.9.
This drove the All Ordinaries Index up 12.5 points to 2,543.2, up from the previous record close of 2,538.1 set on May 16.
Fears about the profit effects of a squeeze on Australian lending margins had pushed the banks index down almost five percent in the past week from a May 13 closing high of 4,562.1.
Brokers said investors buoyant after the U.S. Federal Reserve's inaction and the Dow's rise on Tuesday rushed in to snap up banking stocks, seen as undervalued after their week-long slide.
Resources stocks, which had benefitted from switching away from the banks in the past week, were steady to lower as profit-takers moved in.
The All Resources Index closed down 4.2 points at 1,480.7.

Broken Hill Pty Co, Australia's largest listed company which has risen over seven percent in the last week on the banks-to-resources switch, closed 11 cents down at A$19.15 having leapt in early trade to a year high of A$19.41.
Profit-takers also gnawed away at CRA, which closed unchanged at A$21.12 having earlier risen to a year high of A$21.18.
Late morning wages data described by Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith as too high for a low inflation climate helped take the shine off the initial rally.
The local bond market sold off after private wages data for the March quarter showed 4.8 percent growth.
The 10-year bond yield closed up two basis points at 7.68 percent after the wages data disappointed bond-holders hoping for another local rate cut.
Highlights amoung the smaller stocks included the 18 cent rise by white goods maker Email Ltd to A$4.06 after a five week strike at its Martin Bright steel plant ended.
